BIOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.

19. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

20. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

21. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

22. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
